facts.statement: The beta-tubulin promoter in Ciona robusta is a common marker for neurons but has not often been used to directly observe neural activity.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Researchers created two genetic tools for imaging calcium signals using the beta-tubulin promoter.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Larvae with the first construct displayed glowing signals across their entire nervous system.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The second construct placed a calcium sensor in the cell nucleus and a red protein in the cell body, allowing the red signal to correct for changes in the calcium signal.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Both tools allowed the researchers to see when neurons were activated.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The study shows these two tools work well for imaging neurons in Ciona robusta.
facts.subject: animals
